objective: Test whether startup prewarming a single-image static-cache request with the production discovery prompt width and generation budget removes the first post-restart latency tail without changing semantics or annotation state.

baseline.interpretation: The recurring first post-restart discovery path is about 30 to 33 seconds; later uncached images are about 15 seconds.

latency_gate.reason: Matching prompt width and max token budget did not remove the first production request tail; the observed change versus the paired 29.972 second baseline is within single-sample variation.

controlled_switch_record.attempt_1: Rejected before model load because the old CUDA process had exited but remained in the driver compute list; the original source was automatically restored.
controlled_switch_record.attempt_2: Rejected before serving because the real processor measured 812 prompt tokens rather than the expected 894. The old source hash was restored; a second driver-release race required a bounded manual restart of the already-restored old source.
controlled_switch_record.attempt_3: The corrected candidate became healthy and met the 894-token startup contract, then failed only the live latency gate.
controlled_switch_record.rollback: The same ownership, in-flight, GPU-idle and health checks restored the previous source and waited for the previous health contract before returning.

next_direction: Do not repeat prompt-width-only prewarming. The remaining tail likely depends on the full discovery schema, constrained-decoder path, or longer decode trajectory; any next candidate must preserve the exact request and pass the same semantic hash and under-25-second first-request gate.
